subject: Private deployment: patching schedule, canary & rollback runbook
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@mavenhealth.com>; ops@mavenhealth.com
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment: patching schedule, canary & rollback runbook

Hi Sara / Maven ops team —

Following our call last week, I'm proposing an initial maintenance plan for the private deployment in your VPC so we can apply the 1.2.3 security patch and the runtime optimizations we discussed. High level:

- Target window: Saturday, Nov 14, 02:00–06:00 UTC (4h) — primary region US-WEST.
- Canary: 1 host (single GPU) in us-west-2 → 2h validation window before broad rollout.
- Version pinning: will pin to release tag redwood-private-1.2.3 for the rollout; we will keep previous release (1.2.2) available in the image registry for immediate rollback.
- Rollback: automated image revert + KV cache flush + warm-up script we provide.
- Tests: smoke (sanity), latency p95, inference correctness checks against your representative prompt set.

I'm attaching a draft runbook and the canary checklist. Can you confirm the maintenance window constraints on your side? If Nov 14 is problematic, please propose an alternate weekend.

Notes for internal folks (cc'd): Dev — please review the rollback steps in the runbook around cache invalidation and the compatibility note for quantized weights. Irene — I will need a quick patch to the healthcheck endpoint to surface cache warming progress.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_private_patch_runbook_v1.2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: canary_checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@mavenhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@mavenhealth.com; Infra Partner <infra@consult.co>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:26:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: patching schedule, canary & rollback runbook

Thanks Michael — appreciate the level of detail. Quick notes from our ops team: 

- Weekend windows are OK but we have a hard constraint for production in APAC: for our US tenancy, the preferred window is Saturday 02:00–05:00 UTC (3h).
- We need the canary validation to include a synthetic workload that mirrors our peak short-burst traffic; we'll provide a small generator.
- Security asked for an audit trail of the actual binary/image digest that gets deployed (not just the tag).

We can do Nov 14 as long as you reduce the broad rollout to 60 minutes after canary validation (i.e., total max 3h). We also require a rollback-to-clean-state procedure documented with exact commands for our infra team to run under time pressure.

Can you update the runbook to include: exact image digests, a documented step-by-step rollback, and a short checklist for our SOC to sign off on (post-patch verification)?

Sara
Sara Bennett
Head of Platform Ops, MavenHealth
[Signature]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@mavenhealth.com>; ops@mavenhealth.com
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: patching schedule, canary & rollback runbook

Sara — thanks for the constraints. I've updated the runbook PDF to include the exact SHA256 digests we'll deploy and a one-page "Rapid Rollback" quick reference with commands to revert images and restore prior nomad/k8s workloads. Highlights below: 

- Canary window: 60 minutes validation (we'll run the synthetic workload you provide). If canary passes, automated canary rollout script will expand to the pinned pool with a 60-minute progressive window (so total 2h of active deployment).
- Rollback steps (quick ref): 
  1) kubectl set image deployment/redwood-runtime redwood-runtime=redwood-private@sha256:<rollback-digest>
  2) run cache-warm.sh --warm-from=1.2.2 --parallel=4 (script included)
  3) verify health endpoint /_runbook/status returns OK and cache_warmed=true

- Audit: each deployment will emit the deployed digest to /_internal/deployments/log and we will push the same entry to the shared Drive link (see related links).

I've also attached a canary checklist spreadsheet with the specific metrics we'll watch: error-rate, p95 latency, tokens/sec, and model output diff rate vs baseline. Stephanie — can you confirm SLO thresholds that we should automatically treat as a failure during canary?

Attached: updated runbook v1.2 (PDF), canary checklist.

Best,
Michael
[Attachment: redwood_private_patch_runbook_v1.2.pdf (updated)]
[Attachment: canary_checklist.xlsx]

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>; irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@mavenhealth.com>, ops@mavenhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-05T11:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: patching schedule, canary & rollback runbook

FWIW, a few technical clarifications (kept short):

- Cache/KV considerations: the new runtime sets a different cache alignment for quantized KV blobs. Rolling forward is safe, but rolling back requires a forced KV cache purge on hosts that saw the new runtime (we've included that in cache-warm.sh). Without purge you can see ephemeral correctness mismatches until the cache is rebuilt.
- Network: the maintenance will open port 5201 between the redwood control agent and the model shard containers for a short window during the migration; ensure your firewall rule allows that for the canary host.
- DB migrations: there is no heavy DB migration in 1.2.3, only a tiny schema tweak to the deployment metadata table; migration is backward compatible for reads, but write-after-migration will emit a minor extra column. We recommend taking an export snapshot before the rollout.

I'll be on-call the night of the rollout for live troubleshooting. Adding a short test step to the checklist: after rollback, run the prompt-diff harness against the last-known-good baseline.

- Dev

From: Sara Bennett <sara.bennett@mavenhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, ops@mavenhealth.com, Infra Partner <infra@consult.co>
Date: 2026-11-07T14:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: patching schedule, canary & rollback runbook

Michael / team —

Thanks, all of that looks good. Confirming:

- Nov 14, 02:00–05:00 UTC confirmed for MavenHealth US tenancy (3h). Canary will be 02:00–03:00 UTC; broad rollout 03:00–04:00 UTC with a 1h buffer for validation and rollback.
- We accept the rapid rollback quick ref and the exact image digest audit approach.
- Our SOC will perform post-patch verification and sign off via the Drive form you provided.

Action items before Nov 14: 
1) Redwood to provide the final deployment digest + runbook link by Nov 10 EOD (Michael).
2) MavenHealth ops will provide the synthetic workload generator and firewall exception by Nov 9 (ops@mavenhealth.com).
3) Joint test run of canary checklist in staging on Nov 12 (both teams).

We'll add a short Doc with the SOC checklist into the Drive folder. Once the digest is uploaded and we get the staging smoke test pass, go ahead and schedule the run.

Sara
